question: Does one explicitly identified genus-two Jacobian kill the whole inherited Sha block, and how large a rational lifting obstruction does the existing CT matrix certify?
selection: All six existing fixed-cubic controls, with their pinned inherited spaces and complete restricted CT matrices.
checks: Verify the sextic genus-two equation, discriminant, and both degree-two elliptic quotient maps.
Verify the branch labels match the fixed theta to theta+u*theta^2 identification.
Extract a full nondegenerate symplectic subspace of each retained CT matrix and retain all anchor masks.
Apply the exact gluing sequence to prove that these independent Sha classes are killed in one Jacobian.
Keep the resulting rational projection-index obstruction separate from point-search visibility and from a positive rank predictor.
Use only the listed good primes to seek a different Frobenius trace, proving the gluing extension cannot split as an abelian-variety extension.
failure_semantics: Failure to identify the labelled gluing leaves the common-Jacobian conclusion UNKNOWN. A shared Jacobian alone proves no rational point on any cover. If no listed prime distinguishes Frobenius traces, isogeny and extension splitting remain UNKNOWN.
